In past tense it falls on the fin…

sources.citation: Schröder, Helga & Martin Schröder. 1984. The Toposa verb. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 5: 1-47. Juba: SIL / Institute of Regional Languages, Univ. of Juba (2005 SIL-Sudan facsimile).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 1.1 'Phonology' (p. 3) covers only the ten ATR-harmony vowels, voiceless vowels and harmony rules; no word 'stress'/'accent' anywhere in the article. Tone: 'verb tone [is] considered only as far as [it] touch[es] the scope of the paper' (p. 2); p. 9: 'In the past tense, high tone occurs on the final syllable rather than on the penultimate syllable as in non-past'; note 3 (p. 46) says high tone is predictable on the penult in non-past and final in past, 'very tentative'.

sources.citation: Schröder, Helga. 2013. Clause chaining in Toposa: a pragmatic approach. Lodz Papers in Pragmatics 9(1): 25-44 (author copy, Univ. of Nairobi repository).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tone only (tense marked by tone pattern over the verb). 'stress' occurs once, in the sense 'authors stress'. No word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Schröder, Helga. 2002. Word order in Toposa: an aspect of multiple feature-checking. PhD thesis, University of Nairobi. xiv+194 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology chapter; transcription notes pp. 18-19 describe the nine/ten-vowel ATR harmony, word-final voiceless vowels, vowel length, and tones 'high (H) and low (L), a fall (F) at the end of words, and a rise (R) which is rare'; tone marks case on nouns and tense on verbs. No mention of stress or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent the full text: 'prominence' only in syntactic sense).

sources.citation: Schröder, Martin Christian. 2026. Translating unknown concepts into Toposa: a lexical-pragmatic approach. PhD thesis, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Newest long Toposa monograph, open access on the VU portal but the file is behind an automated-access block by automated download; may contain a language-background chapter with a phonology summary.
Vowel harmony, voiceless vowels (citing Schröder & Schröder 1987a: 17, 1987b: 27) and 'Toposa has tone, which is grammatical rather than lexical.' No stress statement.

sources.citation: Schröder, Helga. 2004. Inflection in Toposa: a VSO language in morpho-syntactic theory. Occasional Papers in Language and Linguistics (Univ. of Nairobi) 2. 16 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only tonal remarks (tense marked by a tone pattern over the whole verb; nominative tone pattern HMF on nyaberu 'woman'). No stress statement.

sources.citation: Schröder, Martin C. 2004. Issues in Toposa orthography. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 27-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.4 Tone (p. 30): 'Tone in Toposa is grammatical rather than lexical. Tone patterns extending over phonological words mark case in nouns and tense in verbs.' Nothing on stress or accent in the whole paper.
